dedupe_keys.name: dalton indoor air quality dataset with activities of daily living in india

description: DALTON is a dataset of indoor air quality measurements with occupant-labelled activities from India, described in a 2024 arXiv paper by Prasenjit Karmakar, Swadhin Pradhan and Sandip Chakraborty. It has spatiotemporal readings from 30 indoor sites over six months across summer and winter, in four regions of rural, suburban and urban type, covering studio apartments, classrooms, research laboratories, food canteens and homes. Custom ESP32-based sensors sample once a second and record temperature, humidity, particles of 1, 2.5 and 10 microns, carbon dioxide, nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, volatile organic compounds and ethanol. Occupants gave 3,957 activity annotations through a simple speech-to-text app, from 24 participants among 46 occupants, and site metadata sits in a Metadata folder; identifiers are anonymised. Access: the GitHub repository, free to download. Licence: the paper says the data can be used under the GNU Affero General Public License for non-commercial purposes, and participants consented to the use. Caveats: missing data from power and network outages need cleaning and imputation, and 30 sites is a small sample. Useful for indoor pollution and ventilation analysis, exposure forecasting and building design planning; related records are not yet linked.
